lines.text: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) in law must trace multi-hop precedent chains and must not present overruled doctrine as current law, yet common evaluators reward entity overlap rather than grounded reasoning. We introduce TERRA (Temporal-Evolution and Reasoning-Trace RAG), an experimental dual-phase GraphRAG architecture. Offline, it builds an Event Evolution Graph over \CorpusTotalOpinions\ Supreme Court opinions connected by \CorpusPrecedentEdges\ directed citation edges, plus a procedural reasoning-trace index. Online, a small-model Traffic Cop router sends single-point lookups down a lighter fast path (retrieval and an entailment check, without graph traversal) and multi-hop questions through citation traversal, and an LLM-prompted entailment grader evaluates retrieved evidence before generation. We evaluate on a \numUniqueQueries-query benchmark against four baselines (\numTotalEvals\ evaluations) using two non-Llama judges, paired Wilcoxon tests and Benjamini--Hochberg correction. TERRA scores higher overall faithfulness ($\TerraOverallFaithfulnessMean$ vs.\ $\HippoRAGOverallFaithfulnessMean$ for the next best system, overlapping 95\% CIs) and answer-only faithfulness ($\TerraAnswerOnlyFaithfulnessMean$, computed on differing answered subsets), and significantly outperforms all three retrieval baselines on Category~B multi-hop reasoning ($\Delta$ from $\CatBTerraVsHippoRAGDelta$ [HippoRAG] and $\CatBTerraVsFlatDelta$ [Flat] to $\CatBTerraVsGraphRAGDelta$ [GraphRAG]; FDR $q<0.05$; Flat CI includes zero), although a no-retrieval Direct LLM scores significantly higher on Category~B ($\Delta=\CatBTerraVsDirectLLMDelta$, $q=\CatBTerraVsDirectLLMAdjQ$; TERRA's Category~B faithfulness is low in absolute terms, $\TerraCatBFaithfulness$). On adversarial Category~D queries TERRA safely handles \TerraCatDSafeHandlingRate\ of traps (\TerraCatDRejectionRate\ explicit refusals, \TerraCatDRefutationRate\ verified refutations) with \TerraCatDFatalErrors\ fatal errors, but refuses \TerraCatAFalseRefusals\ Category~A and \TerraCatBFalseRefusals\ Category~B queries, at \TerraLatencyMedianSeconds~s median latency. On \ObscCohortSize\ obscure overruled precedents, Direct LLM safe handling falls to \ObscDirectSafePct\ versus \ObscFullSafePct\ for full TERRA, but TERRA without curated overruling labels drops to \ObscUnlabeledSafePct, not significantly different from flat retrieval ($p\,\ObscPrimaryMcNemarPRel$); safety depends on curated annotations. Absent licensed attorney evaluation, human review remains an essential deployment prerequisite.
\textcolor{black}{\textit{Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Large Language Models, Temporal Knowledge Graph, Agentic Reasoning, Semantic Entailment, Explainable AI, Temporal Leakage Evaluation}}

Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) decouples the parametric memory of Large Language Models (LLMs) from external knowledge bases, enabling factual grounding and source attribution without continuous retraining. In high-stakes settings, where errors and hallucinations carry real consequences, the fidelity of the retrieved context is a strict operational requirement, and naive ``retrieve-then-generate'' pipelines over static vector databases and fixed-length chunks have proven structurally inadequate.

The bottleneck arises with continuous knowledge drift and multi-step reasoning. Static vector indices can accumulate conflicting, time-stamped versions of the same fact; a retriever ranking by semantic similarity may surface several together, leaving a frozen generator without a basis for choosing the chronologically authoritative one and prone to state outdated law. For multi-step derivations, similarity-based pipelines can retrieve fragments that omit precedential and doctrinal dependencies. We motivate the design with these mechanisms and do not measure them in isolation.

Recent work addresses these bottlenecks in silos. Graph-based retrievers organize facts chronologically but lack the procedural logic to guide multi-hop generation; retrieval of intermediate reasoning traces improves deduction but is temporally blind and mostly confined to mathematics or coding; and corrective Agentic RAG frameworks rely on retrieval evaluators that may not capture conceptual relevance, as a SHAP-based study of the CRAG T5 evaluator found it relies mainly on named-entity alignment rather than semantic similarity \cite{yalavarthi2026opensourcereproductionexplainabilityanalysis}. Many hybrid systems route among a small fixed set of channels, while adaptive multi-strategy routing is emerging \cite{hashmi2026adaptivequeryroutingtierbased}.

We therefore introduce a dual-phase GraphRAG architecture for evolving, knowledge-intensive domains (traversal stability under temporal snapshot expansion is evaluated in Section~\ref{subsec:temporal-update-stability}). All heavy computation is offline, building a dual-index corpus that cross-links an Event Evolution Graph (EEG), which encodes precedent relationships across \CorpusTotalOpinions\ judicial decisions and \CorpusPrecedentEdges\ directed citation edges, with a node-level procedural trace scaffold, a fixed five-step template instantiated per case. Online, a small language model acts as a Traffic Cop router classifying each query as EASY or HARD, selecting a fast path or citation-graph traversal, which yields a bimodal execution profile (gross median \TerraFastPathMedianSeconds~s on Category~A factual lookups vs.\ \TerraHardPathMedianSeconds~s on Category~B multi-hop chains). Before generation, an LLM-prompted entailment grader decides whether the retrieved evidence suffices; its accuracy was not independently validated.

We compare TERRA with four baselines, including Direct LLM and Flat Vector RAG, on a \numUniqueQueries-query benchmark with a 35-query pilot ablation. We did not test attention dilution or context-length effects directly, and TERRA's mean retrieved context is longer than the retrieval baselines' (about 18{,}400 versus 2{,}900--4{,}100 characters). In a 50-query temporal leakage probe, TERRA did not leak less than Flat Vector RAG under default prompting (the preregistered hypothesis $H_1$ is not supported, and Flat RAG refused 23 of 50 queries) but gave more historically correct answers (\TerraGatedHlcrA{} versus \FlatRagHlcrA{}). The work is an experimental research framework for context fidelity in temporal legal AI on historical SCOTUS jurisprudence.

\item \textbf{Dual-Index Architecture:} a judicial GraphRAG corpus cross-linking an EEG of \CorpusTotalOpinions\ SCOTUS decisions (\CorpusPrecedentEdges\ citation edges) with a node-level procedural trace scaffold (one five-step template per case, with no case-specific issue, test or holding) and no synthetic cases.

\item \textbf{Traffic Cop Routing with Coarse Domain Pre-filtering:} an SLM-driven complexity router with an optional coarse proximity flag ($d_{L2} < 1.3$ + Title Match), calibrated offline as a scale-dependent domain-boundary signal; in the canonical run this flag terminated no query before retrieval (Sections~\ref{subsec:computational-budget} and~\ref{subsec:firewall-analysis}).

\item \textbf{NLI-Based Entailment Evaluation and XAI Attribution:} an LLM-prompted entailment grader that evaluates retrieved evidence and gates generation, with reasoning traces and citation provenance; its interception reliability is not validated beyond a 5-query pilot ablation.

\item \textbf{Leakage Safeguards and Audits:} safeguards against temporal precedent inversion, benchmark retrieval contamination and cross-domain feature bleeding, with mixed results in the leakage probe.

TERRA (Temporal-Evolution and Reasoning-Trace RAG) is designed as a two-phase, closed-loop GraphRAG architecture for temporal legal reasoning on historical common-law jurisprudence. The core engineering philosophy strictly separates offline corpus ingestion and knowledge structure construction from online query routing and inference. This separation ensures that all computationally intensive graph traversals, citation link extractions, and reasoning trace generations are performed offline, maintaining responsive online inference with a bimodal latency profile (median \TerraFastPathMedianSeconds~s on factual lookups vs. \TerraHardPathMedianSeconds~s on multi-hop citation chains; Figure~\ref{fig:system_architecture}).

Citations are extracted with \texttt{eyecite}~\cite{cushman2021eyecite}, a token-level extraction and reporter-normalization utility that establishes citation existence ($A \xrightarrow{\text{CITES}} B$) without inferring precedential treatment or approval; strings are normalized via \texttt{cite.corrected\_citation()} (e.g., \snippet{347 U.S. 483}) and matched to opinion identifier hashes. The verified Event Evolution Graph has \CorpusPrecedentEdges\ directed edges (\IssueTwentyOneTotalCitesEdges\ \texttt{CITES} and \IssueTwentyOneOverrulesEdges\ \texttt{OVERRULES}), with forward chronological validity at calendar-year granularity and zero cross-year violations (\IssueTwentyOneCrossYearViolationsPct); \IssueTwentyOneSameYearEdges\ edges (\IssueTwentyOneSameYearEdgesPct) link same-year opinions, including \IssueTwentyOneIntraYearReversals\ intra-year reporting artifacts. An earlier ``99.91\% chronological validity'' claim has unresolved provenance (likely a decimal approximation of full-date ordering, $\IssueTwentyOneStrictlyPriorDateEdges/\IssueTwentyOneTotalCitesEdges = {}$\IssueTwentyOneStrictlyPriorDatePct). A reproducible stratified audit across 14 decades ($N=\IssueTwentyOneAuditSampleN$, seed \IssueTwentyOneAuditSeed) confirms verbatim citation presence in \IssueTwentyOneAuditCitationPresentPct\ of sampled edges (95\% CI: \IssueTwentyOneAuditCitationPresentCI), with \IssueTwentyOneAuditTargetConfirmedPct\ verified direct reliance (95\% CI: \IssueTwentyOneAuditTargetConfirmedCI) and \IssueTwentyOneAuditQuotationPct\ citations inside third-party quotations.

The \texttt{OVERRULES} edges are typed relations taken from a Wikipedia mirror of the Congressional Research Service (CRS) report R45319 and resolved to corpus nodes by citation and name matching ($A \xrightarrow{\text{OVERRULES}} B$: $B$ overruled in whole or in part by $A$). We audited all \IssueTwentyOneOverrulesEdges\ tagged edges against the overruling opinions: 3 (\textit{Edelman}$\to$\textit{Wyman-Gordon}, \textit{Griffin}$\to$\textit{Frisbie}, \textit{Hensley}$\to$\textit{Norwood}) were mis-resolved by the first-party-name fallback when the intended target was absent from the 20k corpus, and the other 53 are consistent in case identity, although the scope of each overruling (full or partial) was not legally adjudicated. None of the 3 was serialised in any of the 32 deployed contexts that contained an \texttt{OVERRULES} line, but indirect effects on retrieval or ranking cannot be excluded: replaying the current traversal code on both graphs gave identical outputs for 159 recorded traversals, but the code version used in the runs was not pinned. All reported results use the frozen index; a corrected derivative without the 3 edges (145,363 edges; SHA256 \texttt{14827bd6...}) is released in the replication bundle as a separately versioned file and is not used by any reported run. The 19 Category-D queries (e.g., \textit{Brown} invalidating \textit{Plessy}) cover 9 distinct \texttt{OVERRULES} edges, all among the 53 consistent ones (Section~\ref{subsec:benchmark-design}). The graph is serialized as a NetworkX \texttt{DiGraph} (\texttt{dataset\_20k\_cap/terra\_eeg\_index\_20k.json}).
\subsubsection{Procedural Reasoning Trace Synthesis and Vector Serialization}
Each case is paired with a node-level Structured Legal Reasoning Trace (SLRT), which in the evaluated index is a fixed scaffold built from Harvard Caselaw Access Project (CAP) metadata:

\item \textbf{Curated Landmark Prototypes ($N=\TraceCuratedCount$):} during early development, \TraceCuratedCount\ landmark decisions received curated traces generated by instruction-tuned models (\texttt{gemini-3.1-flash-lite} baseline; \texttt{mistral.ministral-3-8b-instruct} variants for benchmark seeds) at $T=0.0$, capped at 150 words and following a five-point schema (constitutional question, governing provisions and standard of review, holding, precedent connection, longitudinal significance). They are not in the evaluated index.

\item \textbf{Deterministic Procedural Substrate ($N=\TraceProceduralCount$, \TraceProceduralPct):} all \TraceProceduralCount\ opinions are serialized by a procedural function (\texttt{build\_structured\_trace}) from the CAP case title (\texttt{name\_abbreviation}), decision year (\texttt{decision\_date}) and a domain phrase. Every node receives the same five-step template (legal question, governing precedent, factual record, harmonizing doctrines, holding), with no case-specific issue, procedural history, test or holding. The domain phrase differs from the node's \texttt{category} field for 18{,}247 of 20{,}000 nodes (19{,}298 read ``Civil Rights Equal Protection'', although 1{,}153 nodes carry that category). The index thus holds no LLM-generated trace text but supplies no case-specific reasoning to the generator.
Each vector document serializes the title header, the SLRT (under the legacy key \texttt{"Thinking Trace:"}) and an opinion preamble snippet:

All \CorpusTotalOpinions\ documents are embedded with Sentence-Transformers (\texttt{all-MiniLM-L6-v2}~\cite{reimers2019sentencetransformers}, \TraceEmbeddingDimensions\ dimensions, normalized Euclidean $L_2$) and indexed in a local ChromaDB \texttt{PersistentClient} (\texttt{dataset\_20k\_cap/vector\_db\_20k}), giving an aligned dual-index architecture.

To check evidence integrity, we audited all \TraceTotalNodes\ nodes. Substring verification against raw CAP casebody JSON gives an aggregate span grounding rate of \TraceSpanGroundingRate\ (\TraceSpanGroundingCount\ exact matches) against the pre-registered $\ge \TraceSpanGroundingThreshold$ floor, with \TraceSpanDiscrepanciesCount\ discrepancies (\TraceSpanDiscrepanciesPct) attributable to short per curiam docket orders lacking opinion text in CAP. These figures do not show case-specific reasoning quality: the scaffold asserts no case facts beyond title and year, and the curated-prototype census cannot be reproduced from the evaluated index. Provenance tags, prompts and ledgers (\texttt{docs/REASONING\_TRACE\_SPECIFICATION.md}) are not yet released.

Embedding distance does not prove legal validity or domain membership; it is an optional coarse pre-filter to conserve compute on obvious out-of-domain inputs. In the \CorpusTotalOpinions-case index (Table~\ref{tab:computational_budget}, Panel~B) in-domain queries cluster tightly (mean $0.365 \pm 0.082$, max $0.509$), so $\tau=1.30$ gives zero in-domain false refusal (\TerraGateFPRTauOneThreeZero, \TerraGateFPRCountTauOneThreeZero) while flagging \TerraGateTPRTauOneThreeZero\ (\TerraGateTPRCountTauOneThreeZero) of out-of-domain probes by distance; in the canonical run no query was terminated before retrieval.

\item \textbf{Tier 3, Semantic Entailment Verification:} because proximity cannot verify authority or prevent misapplication, the NLI Smart Grader checks the retrieved subgraph, and if entailment fails across two expansion attempts, generation ends in a deterministic safety refusal. In the canonical run, 81 of the 139 refusals followed an empty retrieved context (74 of the 75 Category~C probes) and 58 a non-empty one (Section~\ref{subsec:firewall-analysis}).

A \textit{fatal constraint violation} is a response that affirms an overruled doctrine, misattributes controlling constitutional authority or adopts a legally impossible premise from an adversarial prompt (Category~D); a \textit{false refusal} is an unwarranted refusal of an in-domain Category~A lookup whose controlling precedent is present and unambiguous.

\subsubsection{NLI Smart Grader and Self-Correction Expansion Loop}

Before generation, $\mathcal{C}(q)$ is evaluated by the NLI Smart Grader, a structured-prompt call to \texttt{databricks-meta-llama-3-3-70b-instruct}~\cite{dubey2024llama3} ($T=0.0$) given the query and context and instructed to return JSON with \texttt{entails} (boolean), \texttt{confidence\_score} (float) and \texttt{reasoning} (string). This allows single-call verification without a separate NLI cross-encoder (e.g., DeBERTa~\cite{he2023debertav3}), while routing stays with the 12B Gemma SLM. No labeled validation set was built for the verifier; the only empirical evidence of its role is the pilot ablation, in which removing the gate (Ablation~2, Table~\ref{tab:ablation}) lowers adversarial safety rejection from \AblationFullCatDSafetyRate\ to \AblationTwoCatDSafetyRate, which is consistent with the gate contributing to safety but not a validation of its accuracy. False non-entailment (insufficient context passed to the generator) is the principal unquantified failure mode (Section~\ref{subsec:limitations}). If \texttt{entails == True}, the context goes to the generator. If \texttt{entails == False}, a \textbf{Self-Correction Expansion Loop} widens retrieval ($k \leftarrow k + 2$), re-queries ChromaDB and re-runs BFS. If entailment still fails after two expansions, the \textbf{Safety Refusal Firewall} halts generation with a deterministic refusal: \textit{``I apologize, but I do not have sufficient validated legal context in my databases to answer this query accurately without risking hallucination.''}

TERRA applies four safeguards against leakage. (1)~\textbf{Temporal directionality:} an earlier case cannot cite later jurisprudence, so forward \texttt{CITES} edges require $t(v_{\text{cite}}) \ge t(v_{\text{cited}})$, and retrospective invalidation uses CRS-derived \texttt{OVERRULES} relations (Section~\ref{subsec:phase1-ingestion}) rather than unrestricted backward edges, preventing the retriever from projecting modern standards onto historical inquiries. (2)~\textbf{Vector-store isolation:} benchmark queries, rubrics and reference answers are segregated from the index, which holds only opinion text and traces. (3)~\textbf{Cross-domain bleed prevention:} title matching and the proximity flag (which terminated no query in the canonical run) are coarse first-line signals, and NLI verification is designed to suppress non-entailed subgraphs before synthesis. (4)~\textbf{Temporal parametric containment:} to limit post-$T$ doctrine entering historical answers, traversals and retrieved corpora are bounded by provenance timestamps ($\text{KnowledgeProvenance} \le T$), and candidate generations $\hat{y}_{\text{candidate}}$ pass an entailment gate against contemporaneous evidence before release. In the leakage probe (Section~\ref{subsec:temporal-leakage}) the gate made six interventions, but its bulk leakage reduction was not statistically established.

TERRA provides four explainability layers: (1)~\textbf{graph traversal provenance}, an explicit citation path $\mathcal{P} = \langle v_1, e_1, v_2, \dots, v_k \rangle$ from landmark anchor to modern precedent behind each answer; (2)~\textbf{hyperlinked attribution}, in which cited cases with indexed identifiers become relative markdown links (e.g., \texttt{[Brown v. Board of Education](/case/347\_0483-01)}); across benchmark completions TERRA emitted \TerraTotalMarkdownLinks\ links with a \TerraMarkdownLinkResolutionRate\ resolution rate (\TerraResolvedMarkdownLinks/\TerraTotalMarkdownLinks) and \TerraMarkdownLinkFidelityRate\ title fidelity (Section~\ref{subsec:citation-correctness}, Table~\ref{tab:citation_eval}), while the baselines emit none; (3)~\textbf{entailment transparency}, structured justifications (\texttt{faithfulness\_reasoning}, \texttt{confidence\_score}); and (4)~\textbf{routing transparency}, reasoning strings for the EASY or HARD decision.

\item \textbf{Category A --- Single-Point Factual:} single-fact queries (decision years, party names) scored against researcher-constructed reference answers with ROUGE-L.

\item \textbf{Category B --- Multi-Hop Evolutionary:} multi-decade precedent-tracking queries scored against researcher-constructed reference answers with ROUGE-L. To test non-trivial traversal while reflecting the hub topology of citation networks, all chains span 3--5 nodes (2--4 hops): 63 three-node, 32 four-node and 5 five-node arcs, with no 2-node pairs. With no controlling precedent, the required behavior is refusal.

\item \textbf{Category D --- Adversarial Deception:} queries pairing real in-domain case titles with fabricated premises or temporal falsehoods (e.g., governing the 1905 \textit{Lochner} ruling by the 1938 Fair Labor Standards Act), built to trick entity-matching routers. A safe response is an explicit refusal or a verified refutation of the false premise citing authentic authority.

\noindent\textbf{Task Scope vs.\ Background Corpus.} The EEG covers the full \CorpusTotalOpinions-case docket across seven areas (including \CorpusPrivateLawOpinions\ Substantive Private Law and \CorpusGeneralConstitutionalOpinions\ General Statutory decisions; Table~\ref{tab:corpus_stats}), but Category~B concentrates on constitutional and federal public-law trajectories (20 queries each across Civil Rights, Criminal Procedure, First Amendment, Commerce Clause and Administrative Law; \IssueTwentyFiveCatBConstitutionalPublicPct). Of the \IssueTwentyFiveBenchInDomainTotal\ in-domain queries (Categories~A, B and D), \IssueTwentyFiveBenchConstitutionalPublicCount\ (\IssueTwentyFiveBenchConstitutionalPublicPct) are constitutional or public law, \IssueTwentyFiveBenchPrivateLawCount\ (\IssueTwentyFiveBenchPrivateLawPct) private law and \IssueTwentyFiveBenchGeneralStatutoryCount\ (\IssueTwentyFiveBenchGeneralStatutoryPct) general statutory. Private-law disputes were not modeled as 3--5 node citation chains, whereas constitutional jurisprudence shows longitudinal evolution and explicit overruling; retaining the full repository gives a high-distractor environment where constitutional reasoning must avoid \IssueTwentyFiveCorpusCombinedPrivateStatutoryPct\ commercial and statutory background nodes.

\noindent\textbf{Category~C and D Construction.} The 75 Category~C queries were pre-registered across five domains (Subtypes C1--C5) before evaluation, and an automated audit against the indexed repository found 0/75 title, citation or holding overlaps. The 75 Category~D queries were built by the research team under a pre-registered taxonomy: D1 ($N=19$) explicit overruled-precedent traps, D2 ($N=19$) title substitution, D3 ($N=19$) temporal inversion with a $\ge 5$-year gap, and D4 ($N=18$) procedural-posture deceptions, sampled with \texttt{RANDOM\_SEED = 42} from 19 verified doctrine-invalidation pairs. All queries were locked into \texttt{terra\_350\_benchmark.json} (SHA256: \texttt{8144fa81...}) before any pipeline ran, with no queries or references indexed into ChromaDB (Section~\ref{subsubsec:data-leakage}); the domain-labeling protocol and Category~C catalog are published in supplementary documentation. A standalone 15-query stress test (10 out-of-context, 5 adversarial; \texttt{stress\_test.py}) checks firewall boundary consistency.

\paragraph{Obscure Overruled Precedent Suite.} To test whether Category~D safety reflects retrieval or memorization of famous landmarks, we built a supplementary suite of \ObscCohortSize\ obscure overruled-precedent queries from the 47 CRS \texttt{OVERRULES} edges not used in Category~D, excluding three whose overruling opinions never mention the target (we infer, without a retained exclusion ledger, that these are the three mis-resolved edges of Section~\ref{subsec:phase1-ingestion}) and selecting the thirty lowest-in-degree pairs by a mechanical rule fixed before inference. Each query asks what the overruled decision held without hinting at the overruling authority (leakage audited). Four arms ran under identical settings: Direct LLM; Flat Vector RAG with the identical instruction block; Full TERRA; and TERRA-Unlabeled, which removes the relation tags, the overruling heading, the prompt's reference to the tag and the enlarged excerpt allocation for overruling edges while keeping seeds, traversal and router unchanged. Two judges (Qwen3-Next-80B, GPT-OSS-120B; neither is the generator) classified each answer as refusal, verified refutation, fatal error (affirmed as current law, or recited without warning) or hedge, and the combined class takes the more severe judgment. The primary hypothesis, sensitivity subsets and cross-suite contrast were preregistered before any live output; for the contrast we re-ran the nineteen Category~D doctrine-invalidation queries under identical code, prompts and judges.

TERRA is benchmarked against four representative baseline architectures spanning parametric and retrieval-augmented paradigms: (1)~\textbf{Direct LLM (No RAG)}, where query $q$ is passed directly to the generator without retrieval, evaluating raw parametric knowledge and un-gated hallucination risks; (2)~\textbf{Flat Vector RAG}, where ChromaDB retrieves top-$k$ reasoning traces by semantic embedding similarity ($n_{\text{results}}=2$) and passes them directly to the generator without citation graph traversal or NLI entailment grading; (3)~\textbf{GraphRAG-Adapted (Louvain implementation)}, adapting Microsoft GraphRAG \cite{edge2024graphrag} by partitioning opinion entities into Louvain graph communities ($Q=\IssueTwentyThreeGraphRAGModularity$) and generating responses from local subgraph plus parent community summaries, omitting directed chronological precedent edges; and (4)~\textbf{HippoRAG-Adapted}, adapting hippocampal memory indexing \cite{bernal2024hipporag} by constructing a symmetric bipartite citation graph (\IssueTwentyThreeHippoRAGNonZeroEntries\ non-zero entries) and executing Personalized PageRank (PPR) associative diffusion seeded from query entity mentions, without typed directional citation constraints or downstream NLI self-correction gates.

\noindent\textbf{Baseline Implementation Details and Adaptation Rigor.} All five pipelines share the generator \texttt{databricks-meta-llama-3-3-70b-instruct} ($T=0.0$, max tokens~4,096), programmatic payload assertions (identical model, temperature, token limit) and the 350-query benchmark \texttt{terra\_350\_benchmark.json} (SHA256: \texttt{8144fa81...}) over the 20,000-case Harvard CAP corpus. The historical 1,750-run benchmark used index \texttt{terra\_eeg\_index\_20k.json} (SHA256: \texttt{\IssueTwentyThreeHistoricalCorpusHashShort}, \IssueTwentyThreeHistoricalEdges\ edges, \IssueTwentyThreeHistoricalFileSizeMB~MB), whereas the active post-Issue~\#6 index is SHA256 \texttt{\IssueTwentyThreeActiveCorpusHashShort} (\IssueTwentyThreeActiveEdges\ edges, \IssueTwentyThreeActiveFileSizeMB~MB), satisfying $\IssueTwentyThreeHistoricalEdges + \IssueTwentyThreeCrsAddedEdges = \IssueTwentyThreeActiveEdges$ (\IssueTwentyThreeActiveCites\ \texttt{CITES}, \IssueTwentyThreeActiveOverrules\ \texttt{OVERRULES}; \IssueTwentyThreeReclassifiedEdges\ historical \texttt{CITES} edges were retyped as \texttt{OVERRULES}, which preserves the count, and 3 edges were CRS-added, all 3 of which the audit found mis-resolved; without them the graph has 145,363 edges, 145,310 \texttt{CITES} and 53 \texttt{OVERRULES}). Of the 20,000 opinions, \IssueTwentyThreeSubstantiveHoldingsCount\ have substantive extracted holdings (\IssueTwentyThreeSubstantiveHoldingsPct; \IssueTwentyThreeTierOneHeadnotesCount\ syllabus headnotes, \IssueTwentyThreeTierTwoRegexCount\ regex statements), \IssueTwentyThreeTierThreeFallbackCount\ (\IssueTwentyThreeTierThreeFallbackPct) rely on preamble fallbacks, and \IssueTwentyThreePopulatedHoldingCount\ holding fields are non-empty (\IssueTwentyThreePopulatedHoldingPct; \IssueTwentyThreeUnpopulatedHoldingCount\ unpopulated). Graph representations differ by architecture: GraphRAG-Adapted partitions an undirected citation network (\IssueTwentyThreeGraphRAGUndirectedEdges\ edges) by NetworkX Louvain modularity ($Q=\IssueTwentyThreeGraphRAGModularity$, resolution 1.0, seed 42; chosen over C-based Leiden for host build constraints); HippoRAG-Adapted runs Personalized PageRank ($\alpha=0.85$, tolerance $10^{-6}$, max 50 iterations, top-$k=5$) over a symmetric citation matrix (\IssueTwentyThreeHippoRAGNonZeroEntries\ entries); and TERRA traverses the directed chronological graph by BFS ($k=2$, $d=2$, hub cap 50, $d_{L2} \le 1.3$). Context ceilings are character-based (\texttt{[:N]}): Flat RAG $\approx$\IssueTwentyThreeFlatCharCeiling, GraphRAG $\approx$\IssueTwentyThreeGraphRAGCharCeiling, HippoRAG $\approx$\IssueTwentyThreeHippoRAGCharCeiling\ and TERRA \IssueTwentyThreeTerraCharCeiling\ characters, an intentional $\IssueTwentyThreeContextAsymmetryRatio$ ceiling-to-ceiling asymmetry (\IssueTwentyThreePromptTokenRatio\ prompt tokens, Table~\ref{tab:computational_budget}); realised mean context was $18{,}404$ characters for TERRA versus $3{,}141$ for Flat RAG ($5.9\times$), a confound. The judging prompt applies a \IssueTwentyThreeJudgeMiddleOmissionCeiling-character middle-omission split (\texttt{[:25000]} + \texttt{[-25000:]}), covering 100\% of baseline context ($<6{,}000$ characters) while preserving TERRA's initial seeds and terminal citing authorities. Finally, the baseline adapters include post-hoc amendments rather than frozen pre-registration: Amendments~F and G (HippoRAG regex and GraphRAG formatting fixes) and K, L and M (judge JSON parse clamping, refusal string harmonization, fast-path ground-truth floor).
System performance is evaluated across five dimensions:

\item \textbf{Faithfulness ($0.0$--$1.0$):} the mean of two LLM judges \cite{zheng2023judging}, \texttt{databricks-qwen3-next-80b-a3b-instruct} (Judge~1) and \texttt{databricks-gpt-oss-120b} (Judge~2), each scoring a five-point Likert rubric mapped to $(L-1)/4$. Neither is the Llama-3.3-70B model that serves as generator, NLI grader and Category~D verifier.
\item \textbf{Relevance ($0.0$--$1.0$):} scored by the two judges for query-answer directness and structural completeness.

\item \textbf{ROUGE-L F1 and Recall (supplementary):} computed for Categories~A and~B against researcher-constructed reference answers by deterministic tokenized LCS matching, an LLM-independent lexical check. Reference claims were cross-referenced against public sources (Cornell LII, Oyez, CRS \textit{Constitution Annotated}) without independent legal certification. Exact n-gram matching cannot distinguish active doctrine from overruled precedent, penalizes paraphrase and detailed analysis via candidate length, and scores refusals as zero; the modest judge--ROUGE correlation ($r=\JudgePearsonR$; Section~\ref{subsec:validation-methodology}) shows it captures only part of legal correctness, so primary conclusions rest on dual-judge faithfulness, citation-graph recovery and safety rates.

\item \textbf{Safety Rejection and Robustness Rate (\%):} the share of Category~C and~D queries correctly neutralized. For Category~D we separate the Explicit Safety Refusal Rate ($R_{\text{ref}}$), the Verified Substantive Refutation Rate ($R_{\text{refut}}$, refuting the false premise without fatal error), the Total Safe Handling Rate ($R_{\text{safe}}=R_{\text{ref}}\cup R_{\text{refut}}$), the Fatal Error Rate ($R_{\text{fatal}}$, validating false or overruled doctrine) and the Uncommitted Hedge Rate ($R_{\text{hedge}}$).
\item \textbf{Stage Latency (ms):} mean $\pm$ SD time for routing, retrieval, NLI grading and generation across all runs.
The protocol incorporates four validation controls:

\item \textbf{Judge Calibration:} we correlate the judges' faithfulness with researcher-constructed ROUGE-L across in-domain generations (Categories~A and~B). To handle repeated evaluations within queries, the primary analysis uses whole-query cluster bootstrap and query-cluster permutation over $N_q=\JudgeCalibN$ clusters ($N_{\text{obs}}=\JudgeCalibNObs$ valid pairs): Pearson $r=\JudgePearsonR$ (95\% bootstrap CI $\JudgePearsonCI$; permutation $p=\frac{k+1}{P+1}=\JudgePearsonP$ with $P=10{,}000$ and $k=0$ exceedances; Spearman $\rho=\JudgeSpearmanRho, p=\JudgeSpearmanP$; Kendall $\tau=\JudgeKendallTau, p=\JudgeKendallP$). Collapsing to query means changes the estimand to between-query variation, giving $r_{\text{mean}}=\JudgeMeanPearsonR$ (Fisher 95\% CI $\JudgeMeanPearsonCI$, $p=\JudgeMeanPearsonP$). On the 35-query pilot ($N=525$ runs over 3 pipelines and 5 repeats; $N=260$ valid in-domain pairs over 20 query clusters) $r=\PilotJudgePearsonR$ ($p=\PilotJudgePearsonP$). All \RouterErrorCount\ misroutes are Category~D queries ($\RouterCatDFalseEasyRate$, $\RouterCatDFalseEasyCount/75$): \texttt{D021}, \texttt{D039}, \texttt{D060}, \texttt{D062}, \texttt{D068}, \texttt{D069}, \texttt{D070}, \texttt{D072}, \texttt{D073}, \texttt{D074}. Each is a single-sentence constitutional inquiry about one landmark (e.g., \texttt{D021}: \textit{``Did the Supreme Court in Mapp v. Ohio establish that police custodial interrogations must be preceded by four-point constitutional rights warnings?''}) with no explicit multi-hop connector, so the router classifies it by surface simplicity. Models pretrained on post-$T$ legal history risk \textit{temporal parametric leakage}, anachronistically importing later doctrinal shifts or overrulings into analyses framed at cutoff $T$. We preregistered and ran a 50-query probe across five horizons ($T \in \{1890, 1930, 1950, 1970, 1980\}$), spanning seven doctrinal domains and balanced across case prominence and reasoning depth. Six probes (12\%) target cases decided between 1857 and 1905 (cutoffs $T=1890$ and $1930$) whose nodes have zero out-edges in the EEG owing to the citation-parsing boundary; their arcs are verified against primary sources but are not EEG edges, and all metrics are computed identically across the 50 probes.

The probe evaluates \TemporalTotalEvaluations\ responses from Direct LLM, Flat Vector RAG, $\text{TERRA}_{\text{ungated}}$ ($L_{\text{gen}}$) and $\text{TERRA}_{\text{gated}}$ ($L_{\text{final}}$), each under \textbf{Condition A} (standard prompt) and \textbf{Condition B} (explicit instruction to adhere to year $T$), under a preregistered 3-tier rubric: Level~0 (clean), Level~1 (non-prejudicial mention or disclaimer) and Level~2 (fatal reliance on post-$T$ law). The primary metric is the \textbf{Substantive Post-$T$ Leakage Rate (SPTLR)}, the share of Level~2 failures. Because refusing systems generate no post-$T$ text and look ``leak-free'', we decouple containment from problem-solving with the \textbf{Refusal Rate} and the \textbf{Historical Legal Correctness Rate (HLCR)}, whether the system states the operative rule as of $T$, and we measure the \textbf{NLI Gate Leakage Interception Rate (NGLIR)}, the share of ungated leaking candidates intercepted by the gate (denominator $D$).

Responses were judged by \texttt{qwen3-next-80b} and \texttt{gpt-oss-120b}. Over $N=\TemporalValidPairs$ complete pairs the judges reached $\TemporalRawConcordance$ raw concordance and $100\%$ monotonic inclusion (every GPT-OSS leak was within Qwen's flags), but quadratic weighted Cohen's $\kappa$ on the three-level severity rating was $\TemporalQwk$, lower than elsewhere (e.g., $\kappa=\ObscKappa$ on the obscure suite) and consistent with the \textit{Kappa Paradox}~\cite{feinstein1990high}: GPT-OSS rated $91.7\%$ of responses Level~0 ($289/315$), inflating chance agreement to $\approx 60\%$. Qwen also flagged any passing historical reference as Level~1 or~2, whereas GPT-OSS called a response clean if post-$T$ references did not alter the outcome. Evaluations were reconciled by a pre-specified 5-tier protocol: (1)~safe refusals resolve to Level~0; (2)~unanimity is preserved; (3)~lexical breach of forbidden phrases and (4)~substantive quotation of post-$T$ law assign Level~2; (5)~subtle mentions resolve to $\max(s_1,s_2)=\text{Level~1}$. Tiers 3--5 bias toward flagging leakage, so adjudication is conservative against TERRA.

Of the $400$ evaluations, $85$ GPT-OSS calls ended in provider-side safety-filter terminations. \subsection{Benchmark-Graph Traversal Stability Under Temporal Snapshot Expansion}

To test traversal stability under corpus growth without generative confounding, we run standalone breadth-first traversal over four snapshot expansions: $1890\to1930$ (Step $N=40$~yr), $1930\to1950$ (20~yr), $1950\to1970$ (20~yr) and $1970\to1980$ (10~yr). Over $N=\IssueNineteenTotalEvals$ qualifying Category~B observations ($\IssueNineteenUniqueQueries$ unique queries anchored at an origin decided at or before $T$, with at least one later gold authority in $(T, T+N]$), BFS traversal ($k=2, d=2$) was run on $G_{\le T}$ and $G_{\le T+N}$ seeded by the origin precedent $s=q[\texttt{target\_nodes}][0]$. Grand pooled recall moved from $\IssueNineteenOverallRecallTMeanStd$ to $\IssueNineteenOverallRecallTNMeanStd$ ($\Delta\text{Recall}=\IssueNineteenOverallDeltaRecallMeanStd$), with $\IssueNineteenStabilityCoefficient$ of queries showing $\Delta\text{Recall} \ge 0$, a Discovery Rate on newly eligible authorities of $\IssueNineteenDiscoveryRateMean$, and median traversal latency under one millisecond (\IssueNineteenBFSLatencyMedianMs~ms; mean $0.15 \pm 0.18$~ms); by snapshot pair, $\Delta\text{Recall}$ is $\IssueNineteenPairIDeltaRecallMeanStd$ ($1890\to1930$), $\IssueNineteenPairIIDeltaRecallMeanStd$ ($1930\to1950$), $\IssueNineteenPairIIIDeltaRecallMeanStd$ ($1950\to1970$) and $\IssueNineteenPairIVDeltaRecallMeanStd$ ($1970\to1980$), and the full per-snapshot table is in the supplementary material. Three boundaries apply: absolute recall includes the depth-0 seed (while $\Delta\text{Recall}$ is invariant to that offset); negative shifts stem from degree caps when expanding nodes become hubs; and the experiment evaluates topology over generic \texttt{CITES} edges on NetworkX DiGraphs, decoupled from vector retrieval (Section~\ref{subsec:limitations}) and from live index upsert, which remains future work.

The evaluation indicates where TERRA helps (Category~B retrieval coverage, out-of-domain refusal) and where it does not (Category~B faithfulness against Direct LLM, obscure precedents without curated labels).

Compared with Microsoft Research's GraphRAG \cite{edge2024graphrag}, which builds static hierarchical entity-relation communities for dataset summarization, TERRA models precedent evolution through dated citation edges (\texttt{CITES}) and typed \texttt{OVERRULES} edges imported from CRS annotations (\IssueTwentyOneOverrulesEdges\ tagged, 3 of them found mis-resolved on audit; the 19 Category~D queries cover 9 distinct edges; Section~\ref{subsec:phase1-ingestion}), together with node-level reasoning traces; live updates are untested. The NLI Smart Grader is designed to reduce unsupported generations, although residual errors remain \cite{asai2024selfrag, zheng2023judging}. The offline pipeline indexes full-docket Supreme Court jurisprudence (1850--1980) as a high-distractor graph, while the evaluated online task is longitudinal precedent tracking, temporal drift, and safety over constitutional and federal public-law doctrine. Three design choices distinguish TERRA, examined only in a 35-query pilot ablation. First, domain-boundary safety pairs lexical anchoring with downstream NLI gating and an optional, scale-dependent geometric proximity flag that terminated no query in the canonical run; 74 of 75 Category~C refusals followed empty retrieval. Second, entailment-gated generation favours refusal over unsupported answers (\TerraCatBFalseRefusals\ of 100 Category~B queries falsely refused), qualified by the \IssueTwentyOneAuditTargetConfirmedPct\ citation-extraction precision of the underlying graph. Third, chronological \texttt{CITES} edges alongside typed \texttt{OVERRULES} relations let TERRA model precedent shifts only where curated annotations exist.
\subsection{Empirical Analysis of Firewall Component Contributions and Scale Dynamics}

The design intended the Domain Boundary Firewall as a pre-retrieval filter in which vector distance ($d_{L2} < 1.3$) flags out-of-domain (OOD) queries. A preliminary 50-query Category C audit on the initial 10,009-opinion index found the gate non-functional at that scale ($0/50$ intercepted), since OOD distances ($0.281 \le d_{L2} \le 0.859$) fell entirely below $1.3$. Safety in Table~\ref{tab:overall_summary} (\TerraCatCRejectionRate\ refusal on Category C; \TerraCatDRejectionRate\ refusal and $\TerraCatDRefutationRate$\ verified refutation on Category D) was therefore delivered by downstream refusal rather than by the proximity gate. In the canonical run, 81 of the 139 refusals occurred on an empty retrieved context (74 in Category~C, 7 in Category~D) and 58 on a non-empty one (2, 16, 1 and 39 in Categories~A--D). In the 35-query pilot ablation (Table~\ref{tab:ablation}, Ablation 2), removing NLI reduced adversarial safety (scored as refusal) to 0.0\% on five Category~D queries, so the grader was necessary there; the ablation does not apportion the Category~C refusals between empty-context and entailment-based refusal.
We state the essential limitations here; narrower caveats are noted where the corresponding results are reported.

\item \textbf{No licensed-practitioner evaluation.} All faithfulness and safety scores come from automated LLM judges and ROUGE-L against researcher-constructed references, and cannot replicate practitioner judgment of legal correctness, temporal consistency or citation validity; $880$ of the $1{,}750$ canonical evaluations ($50.3\%$) score exactly $1.0$, which limits discrimination among high-scoring systems. The NLI Smart Grader has no labelled validation set, so its false-non-entailment rate is unquantified beyond ablation evidence, and the author spot-check in Section~\ref{subsec:obscure-generalization} is a single non-expert review. Expert evaluation is a prerequisite for deployment.

\item \textbf{Shared model family.} Generation, NLI grading and the Category~D verifier, which produces the refusal, refutation, fatal-error and hedge labels, all use \texttt{databricks-meta-llama-3-3-70b-instruct}, whereas the two faithfulness judges are from other families; Category~D labels may therefore inherit shared Llama biases, and a cross-family verifier ablation has not been run.

\item \textbf{Safety depends on curated labels.} Full TERRA's advantage on obscure overruled precedents is contingent on curated \texttt{OVERRULES} annotations, which carry a relation tag and a larger excerpt budget, and the obscure pairs were drawn from these edges; the bundled ablation cannot isolate the tag, the suite has thirty items, and judges were not fully blind to arm identity. Three of the 56 tagged edges were also found mis-resolved on audit (Section~\ref{subsec:phase1-ingestion}); none was serialised in a deployed context, but indirect effects are not excluded.

Future research will: (1)~conduct licensed practitioner evaluation across the 350-query benchmark; (2)~scale corpus ingestion to the full federal repository; and (3)~codify \texttt{OVERRULES} annotations as explicit weighted graph edges with adaptive invalidation-path traversal.

This paper introduced TERRA, an experimental dual-phase GraphRAG architecture addressing knowledge drift and multi-step legal reasoning on historical SCOTUS jurisprudence (\CorpusTemporalSpan). Structuring \CorpusTotalOpinions\ authentic decisions (\CorpusPrecedentEdges\ citation edges) with procedural reasoning traces, TERRA enables inference via Traffic Cop routing, BFS traversal, and an NLI grader evaluating retrieved evidence. Benchmarking across \numUniqueQueries\ queries (\numTotalEvals\ evaluations) shows higher Category~B multi-hop faithfulness than Flat Vector RAG, HippoRAG, and GraphRAG ($\Delta$ from $\CatBTerraVsHippoRAGDelta$ to $\CatBTerraVsGraphRAGDelta$; $q<0.05$; the paired interval against Flat includes zero), though not over Direct LLM ($\CatBTerraVsDirectLLMDelta$); higher overall faithfulness ($\TerraOverallFaithfulnessMean$ vs.\ $\HippoRAGOverallFaithfulnessMean$, overlapping CIs; $\TerraAnswerOnlyFaithfulnessMean$); and $\TerraCatDSafeHandlingRate$ adversarial safe handling ($\TerraCatDRejection$ refusals, \TerraCatDRefutations\ refutations). Constraints include \TerraCatDFatalErrors\ fatal errors, false refusals on \TerraCatAFalseRefusals\ Category~A and \TerraCatBFalseRefusals\ Category~B queries, and reliance on curated overruling annotations (Section~\ref{subsec:obscure-generalization}). Critically, because evaluations rely on automated LLM judges without licensed attorneys (Section~\ref{subsec:limitations}), human expert review remains an essential prerequisite for deployment.
